body.p: Please amend the claims as follows. No new matter is added.

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A propulsor assembly for an Anaircraft, comprising:
a plurality of vertical lift propulsor assemblies,each of theplurality of vertical lift propulsor assembly assemblies comprising:a propulsor connected coupled to the aircraft and driven by an electric motor including a rotor and a stator; and
a cyclic control assembly, wherein the cyclic control assembly comprisescomprising:an actuator, wherein the actuator is an electric actuator; and
a push rod extending through a shaft coupling the rotor to the propulsor, wherein:
the push rod is mechanically connectedcoupledto the actuator and the propulsor;
the push rod is configured to increase a blade angle of the propulsor when in response to a displacement of the push rod is displaced in a first direction; and
the push rod is configured to decrease the blade angle of the propulsor when in response to a displacement of the push rod is displaced in a second direction.
2. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, further comprising an electric motor, the electric motor comprising a stator and a rotor, wherein the rotor is mechanically connected to the propulsor; and wherein: wherein the shaft mechanically coupling the rotor and the propulsor is mechanically connected to the rotor using a shaft, wherein the shaft includes:a proximal end and ;
a distal end mechanically coupled to the propulsor;and
the shaft has a central lumen running extending from the proximal end to the distal end; and, wherein the pushrodpush rod extends at least partially through the central lumen.
3. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 2, wherein the pushrod runs push rod is oriented in parallel to a rotational axis of the rotor of the electric motor.
4. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, wherein the cyclic control assembly further comprises a swashplate rocker, wherein the swashplate rocker mechanically connects the push rod and the actuator.
5. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 4, wherein the swashplate rocker is configured to:
translate movement by the actuator in a first actuation direction into movement of thepushrodpush rod in the first direction; and
translate movement by the actuator in a second actuation direction into movement of thepushrodpush rod in the second direction.
6. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, wherein the cyclic control assembly further comprises a propulsor rocker, wherein the propulsor rocker is mechanically connected to the push rod and the propulsor.
7. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 6, wherein the propulsor rocker is configured to:
translate movement by the pushrodpush rod in the first direction to an increase in the blade angle of the propulsor; and
translate movement by the pushrodpush rod in the second direction to a decrease in the blade angle of the propulsor.
8. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 6,further comprising a propulsor link, wherein:
the propulsor rocker comprises a first propulsor rocker end and a second propulsor rocker end;
the second propulsor rocker end is attached to the push rod; and the first propulsor rocker end is attached to the a propulsor link.
9. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, further comprising a flight controller, wherein:
the flight controller is communicatively connected to the actuator; and
the flight controller is configured to:command the actuator to increase the blade angle of the propulsor; and
command the actuator to decrease the blade angle of the propulsor.
10. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, wherein the propulsor comprises is a monolithic propulsor including a plurality of blades extending radially outward from a hub, the hub and the plurality of blades being formed as a single element.
11. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, wherein the propulsor comprises:
a hub, wherein the hub is mechanically connected to the shaft coupled to the rotor of the electric motor; and
a plurality of blades, wherein each of the plurality of blades are isconnected to and extend extends outward from the hub.
12. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 4-1_, wherein the plurality of blades comprises two blades.
13. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, further comprisingwherein the electric motor comprises:
A-a_first electric motor, the first electric motor comprising a first stator and a rotor,
wherein the rotor is mechanically connected to the propulsorthat interacts with the rotor to drive the shaft; anda second electric motor, wherein the second electric motor comprises a second stator that interacts with the rotor to drive the shaft.
14. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, further comprising a flap mechanism mechanically connected to the propulsor, wherein the flap mechanism is configured to allow the propulsor to rotate about a pivot point of the flap mechanism.
15. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 14, further comprising an electric motor, the electric motor comprising a stator and a rotor, wherein the rotor is mechanically connected to the propulsor; such that the rotor and the propulsor are configured to rotate about a rotational axis, and wherein the flap mechanism comprises:
a base rotatably attached to an the aircraft and configured to rotate about a-therotational axis, wherein the rotor of the electric motor is configured to rotate about the rotational axis; and
a hinge, wherein the hinge connects coupling the base and a hub of the propulsor and, wherein the hinge is configured to allow the propulsor to rotate about the pivot point of the flap mechanism.
16. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 14, wherein the flap mechanism is configured to passively control in-flight transients.
17. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 15, wherein the flap mechanism further comprises a locking mechanism comprising a plurality of springs.
18. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 17, wherein each spring of the plurality of springs is attached to the base of the flap mechanism and the propulsor.
19. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, wherein the actuator is a first actuator, and wherein the cyclic control assembly comprises a second actuator, wherein the second actuator is mechanically connectedcoupledto the pushrodpush rod and is configured to rotate the pushrodpush rod about a transverse axis.
20. (Currently Amended) The propulsor assemblyaircraft of claim 1, further comprising:
a flight controller; and
a plurality of pilot controls, wherein:
the flight controller is communicatively connected to the plurality of pilot controls; and
the first actuator is mechanically disconnected from the plurality of flight pilot controls.
21. (New) The aircraft of claim 1, wherein the first direction and the second direction are substantially parallel to a rotational axis of the electric motor and the propulsor, and to an orientation of the push rod.
22. (New) The aircraft of claim 21, wherein a reference plane corresponding to a chord of the propulsor is substantially orthogonal to the rotational axis, and wherein the blade angle of the propulsor is changed relative to the reference plane of the propulsor in response to movement of the push rod in the first direction or the second direction.
23. (New) The aircraft of claim 15, wherein the hinge includes:
a first hinge coupled on the base and received in a first recess defined in an interior facing surface of the hub, at a first side of the rotational axis;
a second hinge coupled on the hub and received in a second recess defined in the interior facing surface of the hub, at a second side of the rotational axis opposite the first side; and
a rod having a first end extending through the first hinge and into the hub, and a second end extending through the second hinge and into the hub.
24. (New) The aircraft of claim 23, wherein the flap mechanism includes:
a first spring coupled between the base and the hub at a first side of a pivot axis of the flap mechanism defined by the rod; and
a second spring coupled between the base and the hub at a second side of the pivot axis of the flap mechanism defined by the rod, wherein the first spring and the second spring limit an amount of rotation of the propulsor about the pivot axis.
